endorsements.quote: We propose that the next generation of evaluation should include prospective, “silent-mode” clinical trials.

To better reflect clinical reality, future benchmark items should align more closely with end-to-end care, considering the full picture of history, physical examination, diagnostic testing, and care coordination.
Such shared failure modes in model-as-a-judge evaluations underscore the need for human adjudication and heterogeneous (cross-model) graders in meta-evaluation to ensure reliability.

unlisted_practices: Future health AI benchmarks should incorporate authentic clinical data rather than exclusively synthetic conversations.
Future health AI benchmarks should incorporate multimodal data, longitudinal follow-up, and system-level constraints such as EHR latency, alert burden, and interoperability.
Evaluators should conduct prospective, EHR-embedded evaluations linking model behavior to longitudinal patient outcomes to establish clinical utility.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/editorial analyzing OpenAI's HealthBench evaluation framework and discussing what is needed for clinically valid AI evaluation.
